plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the reconstruction of a continuous signal from its discrete samples via convolution, presented as a three-part equation. The left panel shows the discrete sample sequence as blue impulse arrows at regular intervals labeled -T_s, 0, T_s, and 2T_s along the time axis t. The middle panel shows the reconstruction kernel — a sinc-like function with peak value 1 that decays with oscillations — which acts as an interpolation filter. The right panel, separated by an equals sign, shows the convolution result: each blue sample arrow generates a scaled copy of the green kernel (shown as dashed green curves), and all shifted, scaled copies sum together to produce the reconstructed continuous signal (solid red curve) that passes through every sample point. This figure demonstrates that ideal signal reconstruction is a linear superposition process, connecting discrete samples back to the continuous domain through sinc interpolation.

interactionPlan.concept: A continuous signal is reconstructed from its samples by convolving the impulse train with a sinc kernel: every sample drops a scaled, shifted copy of the sinc, and the superposition of all copies is the reconstructed waveform.
elements: Three horizontal panels arranged left-to-right on a shared visual baseline
Convolution operator symbol '∗' (drawn as a small circle/asterisk) between panel 1 and panel 2
Equals sign '=' between panel 2 and panel 3
Panel 1: horizontal black time axis with arrowhead, italic label 't' at right
Panel 1: blue vertical impulse arrows at uniform spacing, positive arrows above axis and negative arrows below axis, heights tracing a smooth underlying waveform
Panel 1: tick labels -T_s, 0, T_s, 2T_s under the sample positions
Panel 2: horizontal black time axis with arrowhead and label 't', vertical axis arrow at center
Panel 2: thick bright-green sinc-like kernel curve, peak value 1 at t=0, decaying oscillating side lobes, label '1' next to the peak on the vertical axis
Panel 3: horizontal black time axis with arrowhead and label 't'
Panel 3: the same blue sample impulse arrows, repeated
Panel 3: one dashed green scaled/shifted sinc copy per sample (amplitude = sample value, centered at sample time)
Panel 3: solid thick red reconstructed curve = sum of all green copies, passing exactly through every blue arrow tip
Optional annotation in panel 3 marking zero-crossings of each sinc copy at all other sample instants
Legend: blue = samples, dashed green = individual sinc contributions, solid red = reconstructed signal

interactions.teaches: How sample spacing relative to the signal's bandwidth controls reconstruction: dense samples give narrow, well-separated sincs and an exact red curve, while coarse samples (past Nyquist) give wide overlapping sincs whose sum no longer matches the original signal — aliasing.
interactions.label: Sampling interval T_s

interactions.teaches: That the red reconstruction is nothing but the pointwise sum of the dashed green sinc copies — hiding the copies leaves a smooth curve, showing them exposes the superposition that built it.
interactions.label: Sinc copies

interactions.teaches: That convolution is a sequential accumulation: the kernel is placed at each sample in turn, scaled by that sample, and added to a running total that grows into the full red envelope from left to right.
interactions.label: Sweep kernel across samples (build the sum)

interactions.teaches: That each sample owns exactly one sinc copy, and that copy is zero at every other sample instant — which is why the red curve passes precisely through every sample tip.
interactions.teaches_note: click a blue arrow to isolate its green copy

demo_steps.title: The three ingredients
demo_steps.narration: On the left, the signal exists only as blue sample impulses; in the middle sits the sinc reconstruction kernel with peak 1. The right panel is their convolution — the continuous signal recovered from discrete data.

demo_steps.title: One sample, one sinc
demo_steps.narration: Hide the sum and look only at the dashed green curves: each blue sample plants a sinc scaled to its own height and centered at its own time. Every copy crosses zero at all the other sample instants.

demo_steps.title: Sweeping the convolution
demo_steps.narration: Step the kernel across the samples one at a time and watch the running total accumulate from left to right — convolution is literally this shift-scale-add process.

demo_steps.title: The sum is the signal
demo_steps.narration: Hide the copies and only the red curve remains: a smooth continuous waveform that passes exactly through every blue sample tip. Nothing was invented — the samples fully determined it.

demo_steps.title: Sampling too slowly
demo_steps.narration: Widen T_s past the Nyquist limit: the sinc copies become broad and overlap heavily, and the red reconstruction now drifts away from the original waveform between samples — this is aliasing.

demo_steps.title: Sampling densely
demo_steps.narration: Shrink T_s: narrow, tightly packed sincs reconstruct the signal almost perfectly. Reconstruction quality is set by sample spacing, not by the kernel's shape.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Reconstruction is not guessing between samples — each sample simply contributes its own scaled sinc that is zero at every other sample, so the sum automatically threads through all samples and is the unique bandlimited signal behind them.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Wide, short, three-panel layout on a white background with a shared horizontal baseline; panels separated by a large '∗' (convolution) symbol and a large '=' sign, both in black. Axes are thick black lines with solid triangular arrowheads and an italic serif 't' at the right end. Panel 1 (left third): blue impulse arrows with triangular heads at uniform spacing, several pointing up with varying heights and two or three pointing down below the axis, heights following a smooth low-frequency waveform; serif italic tick labels -T_s, 0, T_s, 2T_s below the axis near the center. Panel 2 (middle third): a short vertical axis arrow at center, a thick bright-green (lime) sinc curve peaking at 1 on that axis with symmetric decaying side lobes crossing zero at regular intervals; small label '1' just left of the peak. Panel 3 (right third): the same blue impulses redrawn, overlaid by thin dashed lime-green scaled sinc copies (one per sample, negative-amplitude copies flipped below the axis), and a thick solid red curve on top that is their pointwise sum and visibly touches each blue arrow tip. During the sweep animation, the currently active kernel copy should be drawn bolder and the red curve should be drawn only up to the swept position. Keep stroke weights heavy and the palette limited to black, blue, lime green, and red, matching a textbook line-art style.

discrepancies: The whole figure is drawn in a 1200×275 viewBox that renders at roughly half scale in the ~600px content column, so every annotation (−Ts, 0, Ts, 2Ts, the '1', the three 't' axis labels) shrinks to ~7px and is barely legible — far less prominent than the large serif labels in the source.
The tick labels in panel 1 collide: at the default Ts = 0.5 the spacing is only ~22px, so '−Ts 0 Ts 2Ts' run together into an unreadable cluster, unlike the cleanly spaced labels in the source.

The middle sinc kernel is drawn over ±3.6 in t with Ts = 0.5, producing ~7 side lobes per side and a very narrow main lobe; the source shows a broad main lobe with only ~3 visible ripples each side, so the kernel reads much 'busier' than the original.

Panel 1 impulse heights/pattern do not match the source silhouette (source has a distinctly tall arrow at t = Ts, tall at 2Ts, two downward arrows, and an isolated tall arrow at the far right); the generated envelope is different, though the qualitative look is retained.
Large empty area below the figure — the strip artwork occupies only the top third of the canvas, weakening the wide-banner composition of the source.

The source's convolution operator is a plain small open circle at mid-height; here it is fine but the equals sign and circle are drawn tiny relative to the panels, reducing the 'A ∘ B = C' readability at default scale.
evaluation.notes: Composition, mark types, and colour scheme faithfully reproduce the three-panel sinc-interpolation identity with an excellent set of meaningful interactions (step player, Ts slider, copy-visibility toggle, convolution sweep, click-to-isolate), but the artwork is rendered at about half scale so all text is uncomfortably small and the −Ts/0/Ts/2Ts labels visibly collide.
action_items: Reduce the viewBox width (or increase font sizes to ~22–26px in viewBox units) so the −Ts, 0, Ts, 2Ts, '1' and 't' labels render at a comfortable inline size, matching the bold serif labels of the source.
Suppress or stagger panel-1 tick labels when the pixel spacing is below the label width (and always keep '0' and 'Ts' readable) to eliminate the current overlap at Ts = 0.5.
Widen the sinc kernel display window (or clip to ~±3.5 Ts) so the middle panel shows a broad main lobe with ~3 ripples per side like the source, and enlarge the '1' amplitude label.
Tighten the vertical layout (reduce the blank band below the strip) and enlarge the ∘ and = operator glyphs so the three-panel equation reads clearly at default size.

feedback.rationale: The concept, panel decomposition, and interactions are correct; the issues are purely implementation-level (viewBox scale, font sizes, label collisions, kernel window, vertical spacing) that the generator can fix directly.

discrepancies: Panel-1 tick labels (−T_s, 0, T_s, 2T_s) are crammed together, pushed off their ticks and connected with grey leader lines; in the source they sit cleanly and directly beneath their own impulses with no leaders.

The whole figure renders small inside a much taller container (viewBox 880×200 in a ~600×560 area), so all text — especially the subscripted T_s labels and the '1' on the kernel axis — is uncomfortably small compared to the bold, large serif labels of the source.

Default sampling interval (Ts = 0.5 over t ∈ [−1.55, 4.7]) yields ~13 impulses in panel 1 versus ~10 well-spaced arrows in the source, making the left panel denser and more cluttered than the original.

The 't' arrow label of panel 1 sits almost touching the convolution '∘' symbol, and the panel-2 't' nearly touches the '=' sign; the source leaves clear visual separation between panels and operators.

Extra elements not in the source (small axis tick marks, white circles marking sinc zeros, optional grey original curve) add chrome; acceptable pedagogically but they slightly alter the clean look of the original.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful three-panel convolution figure with correct blue impulses, green sinc kernel, and red reconstruction plus a rich, genuinely useful set of interactions; the main weaknesses are cramped, leader-line-tethered T_s tick labels and an overall small rendering that makes all text hard to read at inline size.

feedback.rationale: Concept and panel structure are correct (concept_accuracy 5), but label crowding with leader lines, small viewBox scaling, and default Ts spacing are concrete rendering/layout fixes for the generator.
